articles.summary: The Trump administration is reshaping Washington through more than just White House renovations and statue repairs. New polling from Gallup that quantifies the impact of President Donald Trump’s second-term federal job cuts, his immigration crackdown, and the military mobilization in the nation’s capital finds large swaths of people have been affected by these changes in the district and the broader region. Fifty-five percent of people living in the DC-Maryland-Virginia area said they’ve been negatively impacted by federal job cuts and furloughs — a number that rises when just residents of DC and the nearby Virginia suburbs of Arlington and Alexandria are considered. One-fourth of DMV residents reported being negatively impacted by federal immigration enforcement under Trump, including 43% of Hispanic residents. articles.title: There Is No Plan
articles.author: Nathan Grayson
articles.summary: “What else is there to say?” It’s a sentiment many in the games industry have shared following the news that Microsoft laid off another 268 employees . This after the company gave its headcount a buzzcut to the tune of 1,600 mere months ago. The dismal news just keeps coming. We knew it would, because Microsoft signaled as much. But even within that framework, it’s time to acknowledge that those who’ve deemed themselves worthy of steering the ship have no meaningful long-term plan—nothing overriding or set in stone. Unfortunately, this isn’t just a Microsoft problem. Hit particularly hard by the latest round of layoffs was Halo Studios, which has been demoted from heading up a new entry in the Halo canon to support status. Now a team at Activision will take the reins on the series that’s synonymous with Xbox, a whiplash-inducing pivot that would have been considered unthinkable even a few years ago. Will this lead to a game that shares continuity in terms of tone, story, and feel with what came before? Difficult to say, but it’s a tall order.
